A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MixMin research work, including readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B. Content can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original Pythia language-model pretraining experiments and XGBoost experiments on PCBA bioassays, including performance and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds chemistry baseline comparisons, statistical analyses, and five-trial PIQA results.

M1.justification: Source-specific proxy training, the empirical convex mixture objective, and the entropic-descent procedure in Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The new practical recommendations do not establish a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use SlimPajama sources, PIQA, ARC-Easy, SciQ, OpenWebMath, and the same PCBA molecule and assay pools. The added comparisons and repetitions introduce no new task, domain, or population.

E2.justification: v2 adds random search and RegMix to the chemistry comparisons in Figures 16–17, substantially expanding beyond the natural-mixture data-mixing baseline used there in v1. These methods were already evaluated for language modeling, whose comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The added chemistry comparisons in Figures 16–17 restrict the reported 1279-source evaluation to the first three target assays, while the retained natural-mixture comparison covers ten. Existing splits, metrics, model sizes, and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures 16–17 extend the existing source-count sensitivity analysis to random search and RegMix, examining relative performance with 9, 85, and 1279 sources. Existing compute sensitivity, model scaling, ensembling, and cross-task analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports three-trial results with 95% confidence intervals. v2 adds Welch's t-tests across central language-model comparisons, compute budgets, and model scaling in Tables 3–5, plus a five-trial PIQA report in Figure 18. The original three-trial reports remain; a paper-wide increase in runs is not established.

E6.justification: Original plots and Tables 1–2 are retained, but v2 adds substantial chemistry comparison results showing larger advantages over random search and RegMix as source counts grow, plus five-trial PIQA results. New statistical outcomes include Table 3's p-values of 0.006 for PIQA versus random search and 0.839 for OpenWebMath versus random search; the added evidence does not show uniformly significant differences.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds an explicit derivation of the uniform risk-difference bound from the Lipschitz and approximation assumptions, which v1 asserted more briefly. Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A.1 also explicitly distinguish unconditional CE from conditional losses. The convex reduction and final 2Cε bound remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same convex-reduction, cheap-proxy, and scale-transfer contributions, including the headline 1–5% negative-log-likelihood and 0.03–0.15 average-precision improvements. Added experiments support retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds practical applicability conditions, including proximity of the target to a source mixture and sufficient signal in proxy models, with advice to increase proxy compute until mixtures stabilize. The limitations additionally identify how cheaply proxies can be trained without degradation as an open problem.

D1.justification: Hardware, training hyperparameters, data filtering, and access resources remain unchanged. The RegMix notebook URL printed explicitly in v2 was already the destination of the 'public code' hyperlink in v1.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds Ji et al. (2021), Pedregosa (2016), and Shi et al. (2005), discussing obstacles to applying gradient-based and KKT-based bilevel optimization to the paper's hypothesis spaces. Existing data-mixing positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and the section sequence remain intact. Changes comprise localized explanatory expansions, the practical-conditions list, an Impact Statement, and author and affiliation text updates.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column presentation to the ICML two-column format, with widespread resizing and relocation of figures. Figure 5 changes from a 2×2 arrangement to one row, and Appendix B adds Tables 3–5 and Figures 16–18.

improvement.justification: The added chemistry baselines address a gap in v1's comparisons, while significance tests and fuller proof steps make the evidence easier to assess. The gain is limited by sparse implementation and budget details for the new chemistry comparators and only three reported assays at the largest source count. Overall, v2 provides better validation and transparency without resolving all evidential limitations.
